current.text: Verify that every HTTP response with a message body contains a Content-Type header field that matches the actual content of the response, including the charset parameter to specify safe character encoding (e.g., UTF-8, ISO-8859-1) according to IANA Media Types, such as "text/", "/+xml" and "/xml".

master.text: Verify that every HTTP response with a message body contains a Content-Type header field that matches the actual content of the response, including the charset parameter to specify safe character encoding (e.g., UTF-8, ISO-8859-1) according to IANA Media Types, such as "text/", "/+xml" and "/xml".

predecessors.text: Verify that every HTTP response contains a Content-Type header. Also specify a safe character set (e.g., UTF-8, ISO-8859-1) if the content types are text/*, /+xml and application/xml. Content must match with the provided Content-Type header.

Verify that output encoding preserves the user's chosen character set and locale, such that any Unicode character point is valid and safely handled. ([C4](https://owasp.org/www-project-proactive-controls/#div-numbering))

summaries.body:
The 5.0.0 mapping records V4.1.1 as MODIFIED, moved from 4.0.3 V14.4.1 and covering V5.3.2. V14.4.1 required a Content-Type header on every HTTP response, a safe character set (UTF-8, ISO-8859-1) for text/*, /+xml and application/xml, and that the body match the declared type. That is the clause the current control continues.

The COVERS line points at 4.0.3 V5.3.2, which was about output encoding preserving the user's character set and locale, not HTTP headers. Git events on this ID slot include mb's 2018-11-15 authentication-chapter edit, abhay's 2019-02-11 access-control CWE tagging, and other chapter files. Those are ID-slot reuse after the 5.0 chapter split; the mapping and V14.4.1 predecessor text are the reliable origin.

On 23 Apr 2020 tghosth reworded V14.4.1 in commit a31a7023 to resolve issue #710. Two days later elarlang applied header-naming corrections against #720 (commit 6b3f6356). The 5.0 text then limits the header to responses with a message body and recasts the charset examples as IANA media-type patterns ("text/", "/+xml", "/xml") instead of the 4.0.3 list "text/*, /+xml and application/xml".

Issue snapshots attached to this record do not discuss that header clause: #442 is elarlang's 15 Feb 2019 report that a then-V4.1.1 access-control flexibility requirement duplicated V1.4.2 (vanderaj agreed the next day), and #449 is about V5 output-encoding categories. Those issues belong to other occupants of the ID slot.
